content.introduction: The Housing Portal is your gateway to applying for on-campus housing, selecting your room, and managing your residential experience.

sections.title: Housing Options
sections.content:
Traditional Halls:
- Shared rooms (double or triple)
- Community bathrooms
- Most affordable option

Suite-Style:
- 2-4 bedrooms sharing bathroom
- More privacy
- Small common area

Apartment-Style:
- Full kitchen and living room
- Private bedrooms
- Most independence

Special Communities:
- Honors housing
- Wellness floors
- LGBTQ+ inclusive
- Substance-free

sections.title: Application Process
sections.content:
Timeline:
- February 1: Applications open
- March 15: Priority deadline
- April 1: Room selection begins
- June 1: Final assignments

Steps:
1. Submit housing application
2. Pay $300 deposit
3. Complete roommate questionnaire
4. Select roommate (optional)
5. Participate in room selection
6. Receive assignment

sections.title: Room Selection
sections.content:
How It Works:
- Selection time assigned by credits/class year
- Log in during your window
- Browse available rooms
- Select and confirm your choice

Tips:
- Have backup options ready
- Know your roommate's preferences
- Select quickly - rooms go fast

sections.title: Living On Campus
sections.content:
What's Included:
- Furnished room (bed, desk, closet)
- Utilities (electric, water, internet)
- Laundry facilities
- Common areas
- RA support

What to Bring:
- Bedding (twin XL)
- Toiletries
- School supplies
- Storage containers
- Mini fridge (4.5 cu ft max)

sections.title: Policies
sections.content:
Contract Terms:
- Full academic year commitment
- Early termination fees apply
- Cancellation deadline: June 1

Community Standards:
- Quiet hours: 10PM-8AM weekdays
- Guest policy: Sign in required
- No candles or open flames
- No pets (except fish)

content.conclusion: Apply early for best selection! Contact Housing at (555) 123-4550 with questions.

content.introduction: Campus Dining offers a variety of meal options to fit every taste, dietary need, and schedule.

sections.title: Dining Locations
sections.content:
Residential Dining Halls:
- Main Dining Hall (all-you-can-eat)
- North Campus Dining
- West Campus Dining

Food Courts:
- Student Union Food Court
- Library Cafe
- Athletic Center Grab & Go

Specialty:
- Campus Coffee Shop
- Late Night Express (9PM-2AM)

sections.title: Meal Plans
sections.content:
Unlimited Plans:
- 19 meals/week + $200 dining dollars
- 14 meals/week + $400 dining dollars

Block Plans:
- 150 meals/semester + $300 dining dollars
- 75 meals/semester + $500 dining dollars

Dining Dollars Only:
- Various amounts available
- Accepted everywhere on campus

sections.title: Dietary Accommodations
sections.content:
Available Options:
- Vegetarian/vegan stations
- Gluten-free options
- Halal and Kosher options
- Allergen-free preparation

Allergy Information:
- All items labeled for top 8 allergens
- Ingredient lists available
- Chefs can prepare special requests

Contact dining services to set up accommodations.

sections.title: Hours
sections.content:
Main Dining Hall:
- Breakfast: 7:00-10:00 AM
- Lunch: 11:00 AM-2:00 PM
- Dinner: 5:00-8:00 PM
- Weekend Brunch: 10:00 AM-2:00 PM

Food Courts:
- Mon-Fri: 7:00 AM-10:00 PM
- Sat-Sun: 10:00 AM-8:00 PM

Hours vary during breaks.

sections.title: Tips
sections.content:
Saving Money:
- Choose plan that fits your habits
- Don't let swipes expire
- Bring containers for takeout
- Check for meal deal specials

Food Pantry:
- Free food for students in need
- Student Services Building
- No questions asked

content.conclusion: Questions about your meal plan or dietary needs? Contact Dining Services at (555) 123-4555.

content.introduction: With over 300 student organizations on campus, there's something for everyone. Getting involved is one of the best ways to make friends and develop skills.

sections.title: Types of Organizations
sections.content:
Academic & Professional:
- Honor societies
- Pre-professional clubs
- Major-specific groups

Cultural & Identity:
- International associations
- Cultural heritage groups
- LGBTQ+ organizations

Service & Advocacy:
- Volunteer organizations
- Environmental groups
- Political organizations

Special Interest:
- Sports and recreation
- Arts and performance
- Gaming and hobbies
- Media (newspaper, radio)

sections.title: Getting Involved
sections.content:
How to Find Organizations:
- Attend the Activities Fair (each semester)
- Browse the organization directory
- Ask friends and classmates
- Check bulletin boards

Joining:
- Most welcome new members anytime
- Attend a meeting to learn more
- Some require applications/tryouts

sections.title: Benefits
sections.content:
Personal Growth:
- Leadership experience
- Time management skills
- Public speaking practice
- Networking opportunities

Professional Development:
- Resume building
- Industry connections
- Skill development
- References

sections.title: Starting a New Organization
sections.content:
Requirements:
- Minimum 5 student members
- Faculty/staff advisor
- Constitution and bylaws
- Complete registration form

Process:
1. Develop concept
2. Recruit members
3. Find advisor
4. Write constitution
5. Submit application
6. Present to review committee

Timeline: 4-6 weeks for approval

content.conclusion: Don't wait - get involved early! Contact Student Activities at (555) 123-4580.
